div.head: I Atr 1.7
div.ab: Gif he þonne uhtleape ⁊ þæt ordal forbuge, gylde se borh þam teonde his ceapgyld ⁊ þam hlaforde his were, þe his wites wyrðe sy.
Gyf he ðonne uthleape ⁊ þæt ordal forbuge, gylde se borh ðam teonde his ceapgyld ⁊ ðam hlaforde his were, ðe his wites wyrðe sy.
Si aufugiat et ordalium uitet, reddat plegius eius capitale suum repetenti et domino weram suam, qui ea dignus sit.
Gyf he ðonne uthleape ⁊ þæt ordal forbuge, gylde se borh ðam teonde his ceapgyld ⁊ ðam hlaforde his were ðe his wites wyrðe sy.
If he escapes and avoids the ordeal, his surety shall pay the value of his goods to the accuser and the wergeld of the accused to the lord who is entitled to the fines incurred by him.

Wenn [Verklagt]er aber entflieht und das Ordal vermeidet, so zahle der Bürge dem Kläger dessen Schadenersatz und jenem Herrn, [sofern] der zu dem [durch Verklagten verwirkten] Strafgeld berechtigt ist, des letzteren Wergeld.

But if [the accused] escapes and avoids the ordeal, let the surety pay the plaintiff his compensation for the goods, and the lord — [if] he is entitled to the fine [forfeited by the accused] — the latter's wergild.
div.note: III Atr 6.2; II Cn 30.3b; II Cn 30.6
